change: Represent matrix axis selections with compact IntRange values. Support stepped, reversed, exclusive-first and stored ranges for reads, replacement, scalar fill and dotted updates. Bind open and omitted axes before RHS evaluation; revalidate coordinates using the current destination shape. Specialize one- and two-dimensional traversal and retain bulk contiguous-row copies. Add four-dimensional reshape overloads.
validation: Independent C bootstrap, then 1322 focused numeric, array comparison, compound, slice/index, formatter and reaction checks passed in 40.09s. Ruff and git diff --check passed.
coverage: Forward/backward ranges, saved selectors, inclusive/exclusive endpoints, open descending ranges, per-axis end, dropped axes, omitted axes, empty selections and dimensions.
Rank-one through rank-four matrices; source/endpoint evaluation once in order; saved managed values and repeated-work allocation cleanup.

48 deterministic generated shape/selector combinations per target/mode compare shape, every selected cell, replacement, dotted update and saved copies with an independent Python coordinate calculation.
Dotted update captures its original selectors even when the RHS changes selector variables and reshapes the destination.
Zero steps, negative selected indices, full-domain/wide-stride selectors, wrong replacement lengths and undersized reshaped destinations fail.
Formatter round trips, renderer content and independent scalar reaction-model reference.
additional_fix: The generated empty-array case exposed a pre-existing compiler ICE on `a =? [0] and b =? []`, reproduced with the prior committed compiler. Do not register the immutable null constant as a temporary requiring conditional cleanup: it owns no allocation and cannot be assigned. Add a native/web default/release regression with repeated cleanup checks.
limits: The private matrix selector representation changes; this is not an internal ABI compatibility promise.
Empty ranges select no coordinates, matching ordinary stored array ranges; nonempty ranges validate every selected coordinate without expanding the range.
The implementation still allocates output values, selector metadata and one offset per selected run along the last axis.
Native timing covers only the recorded contiguous-slice and simulation workloads, not general strided-matrix throughput or GPU performance.
Five compile pairs show no material regression in the selected programs.
